A September edit of London portraiture, image culture, autumn campaigns and a new coastal story from Portugal.

London / Fashion / Portraiture

Davide Studios

Monthly Newsletter — September Issue

September turns toward the constructed image: contemporary portrait painting at the National Portrait Gallery, Frida Kahlo’s passage from artist to global icon, and fashion campaigns built from archive, psychological tension and architecture. On the coast of Portugal, Dreamland follows a quieter movement between sunlight, rock, tide and the changing silhouette of a figure.
 

01 — On the Field

Field Notes from the studio: a coastal portrait sequence moving from bright stillness into shadow and motion.

Dreamland: Tide, Light, Silhouette

Dreamland was photographed on the Portuguese coast, where the landscape offered two different emotional registers within the same afternoon. The opening frames hold the subject in warm light and pale fabric, close to the rock and water, with gestures that feel quiet and almost suspended.

01 — Stillness. Dreamland, Portugal, 2026. Photograph: Davide Studios.

The coast is not treated as scenery. Tide pools, stone and open sky give the body a changing scale: intimate in the close portraits, then smaller and more exposed as the frame opens toward the Atlantic.

02 — Tide. Dreamland, Portugal, 2026. Photograph: Davide Studios.

As the wardrobe turns black, the sequence becomes more graphic. Fabric catches the wind, the figure separates from the sand and cliffs, and movement replaces the earlier stillness without losing the sense of concentration.

03 — Silhouette. Dreamland, Portugal, 2026. Photograph: Davide Studios.

The edit moves from ivory to black, repose to motion, and portrait to silhouette. The transition is gradual, allowing light and distance to carry the narrative rather than forcing the landscape into a postcard or the subject into a fixed character.

02 — Art

A London-facing edit for portraiture, photography, contemporary art and the changing language of images.

First Prize: Jean-Denis, 2025 by Marc Dalessio. Courtesy National Portrait Gallery. © Marc Dalessio.

National Portrait Gallery / St Martin’s Place, London WC2H 0HE / 25 June - 7 October 2026

Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer Portrait Award 2026

The annual award brings together contemporary portrait painters working across classical observation and more experimental approaches. This year’s prize winners range from Marc Dalessio’s direct, dark-toned Jean-Denis to Michael Slusakowicz’s chromatic double portrait Charlie and Magda, showing how pose, surface and psychological distance can shift the way a sitter occupies the frame.

Why it matters visually: For photographers, the exhibition is a concentrated study in how expression, gesture, colour and background can build a portrait before technique announces itself.

View exhibition

Tate Modern / Bankside, London SE1 9TG / 25 June 2026 - 3 January 2027

Frida: The Making of an Icon

More than thirty works by Frida Kahlo sit alongside photographs, garments, personal objects and the work of later artists to examine how a painter became a cultural symbol. The exhibition follows the tension between Kahlo’s self-authored identities and the commercial afterlife of her image across politics, fashion, fandom and popular culture.

Why it matters visually: It asks a useful image-making question: when does a portrait remain a person, and when does repetition turn it into an icon or a product?

Book tickets

National Portrait Gallery / St Martin’s Place, London WC2H 0HE / 9 October 2026 - 7 February 2027

Tim Walker’s Fairyland: Love and Legends

Opening in October, Tim Walker’s new exhibition turns portraiture toward folklore, theatrical invention and collaborative world-building. The advance programme positions the show around love, legends and the imaginative spaces created between photographer, sitter, costume and set — a timely preview for anyone interested in fashion imagery as narrative construction.

Why it matters visually: Walker’s practice treats the set as a psychological space, offering a counterpoint to minimal portraiture and a lesson in building images through atmosphere.

Book tickets

Tate Modern / Bankside, London SE1 9TG / 26 September 2026, 11.00-20.00

The Evolving Studio: Artists Working with Technology

This one-day programme brings together a new generation of artists using technology as part of creative practice. Talks, demonstrations and participatory work focus attention on how tools reshape process, collaboration and authorship — not as a separate digital category, but as material that now sits inside the contemporary studio.

Why it matters visually: For photographers navigating AI and computational tools, the event frames technology through artistic intention, process and authorship rather than novelty alone.

03 — Fashion

Three autumn campaigns selected for their use of character, archive, architecture and controlled cinematic tension.

Official McQueen Autumn Winter 2026 campaign image. Photographer and director: Glen Luchford.

McQueen / Current as of 22 September 2026

Autumn Winter 2026: The Artifice Undone

Photographed and directed by Glen Luchford, McQueen’s campaign moves between a meticulously controlled facade and something more tactile beneath it. Karen Elson, Paloma Elsesser, Jacqui Hooper and Xiao Wen hold the frame with confronting stillness while noir light, cinematic staging and sharp tailoring turn the image into a study of performance, interiority and the moment control begins to fracture.

View official source

Official Versace Fall Winter 2026 campaign image from the House campaign page.

Versace / Published 29 July 2026; current September 2026

Versace Obsessed, Chapter II

Versace builds its Fall Winter campaign as a collision between present bodies and the house’s own visual archive. Historic Steven Meisel imagery, magazines and unseen objects sit beside leather, gold, Medusa and Greca motifs. The result is less retrospective than charged collage: glamour and grit, classicism and street language, photographed as inheritance that remains active rather than sealed behind glass.

View official source

Official Paul & Shark Fall/Winter 2026 campaign image. Photographer: Charlotte Lapalus.

Paul & Shark / Current as of 22 September 2026

Elements in Motion

Charlotte Lapalus photographs Paul & Shark at Casa Corberó, using the building’s monumental concrete forms as more than a backdrop. Arches, planes and passages give the clothes a measured rhythm, while movement keeps the architecture from becoming static. It is a useful lesson in location-led fashion imagery: the setting provides structure, but the subject still carries the frame.
